video_title: Trump’s GRIFT Is Unraveling | Jessica Tarlov on Fox News, MAGA, Billionaires, and 2026
gist: Fox News 'The Five' co-host and former Democratic pollster Jessica Tarlov argues the 2026 midterms are shaping up strongly Democratic. In her view corruption (Trump's crypto dealings and the ballroom), tariffs, the Iran war and a 20+ point Democratic healthcare edge are driving Republican erosion, and Democrats are competitive in red-state Senate races (Georgia, Alaska, Texas, Iowa), though she warns of a possible large polling error. The title's 'grift' framing is reflected in her corruption thesis; much of the remaining hour covers communication style and personal chat.

insights.claim: Jessica Tarlov expects the 2026 midterms to be strongly Democratic, saying Republican prospects have 'taken a nose dive' in recent weeks and months, worsened by the war in Iran and Trump's refusal to back off tariffs despite court losses.
insights.speaker: Jessica Tarlov
insights.so_what: A Democratic House/Senate swing raises odds of gridlock, tariff pushback and oversight of the administration, which matters for policy-sensitive sectors.
insights.quote: I feel like the midterms are going to be pretty blue in the political sense.

insights.claim: Tarlov, a former Democratic pollster, warns she fears a large polling error because Democrats showing 10-15 point generic-ballot leads looks implausible given that the Democratic Party itself remains unpopular.
insights.speaker: Jessica Tarlov
insights.so_what: Positioning for a blue wave carries tail risk if polls overstate Democrats; hedge election-outcome trades.
insights.quote: I'm also afraid, even as someone who works in polling, about like a huge polling error. Cuz some of it just seems too crazy.

insights.claim: Tarlov says Democrats are competitive or polling ahead in Senate races in traditionally red states including Georgia, Iowa, Alaska and Texas, with a Republican operative anonymously describing the Georgia strategy against Jon Ossoff as just 'keep the patient comfortable' for challenger Mike Collins.
insights.speaker: Jessica Tarlov
insights.so_what: A broadened Senate map makes a Democratic Senate majority plausible, shifting probabilities on confirmations, tax and trade legislation.

insights.claim: Tarlov reports Mary Peltola was eight points ahead of sitting Republican Senator Dan Sullivan in Alaska, and that a staff-treatment controversy reported by the New York Times has not hurt her because Democrats are now prioritizing winning over purity.
insights.speaker: Jessica Tarlov
insights.so_what: A Democratic pickup in Alaska would be a strong signal of Senate control flipping.

insights.claim: Tarlov cites a new poll showing Texas Democratic House candidate Bobby Polito (a Tejano singer) up 13 or 15 points, and says Republican candidates across the country are dodging debates.
insights.speaker: Jessica Tarlov
insights.so_what: Debate avoidance and outsized House leads point to a broad House swing, not just isolated upsets.

insights.claim: Tarlov describes a 'camo wave' redux: a larger class of veteran candidates than 2018, with the biggest-ever class of female veterans, plus a 'blue-collar brigade' of former firefighters and other working-class candidates, which she sees as appealing in non-traditional Democratic territory.
insights.speaker: Jessica Tarlov
insights.so_what: Candidate quality in swing districts supports the case for a large Democratic House majority.

insights.claim: Tarlov notes the 2024 lesson that higher turnout would have made Kamala Harris lose by more, breaking the Obama-era assumption that more voters means bigger Democratic margins.
insights.speaker: Jessica Tarlov
insights.so_what: Turnout-based models of Democratic strength are no longer reliable; low-propensity voters now lean right.
insights.quote: if more people had voted Kamala would have lost by more.

themes.theme: Corruption as the Dominant Election Issue

insights.claim: Tarlov argues fighting corruption is the single most animating issue of this election across party lines, and that Trump's corruption, from the crypto 'grift' to the White House ballroom, has caught up with him even among Republican voters.
insights.speaker: Jessica Tarlov
insights.so_what: Trump-linked crypto ventures and government-contract beneficiaries face rising political and regulatory scrutiny risk if Democrats gain power.
insights.quote: they stand for, you know, a fight against corruption, which I think is the most animating element of this election, no matter how you're going to vote.

insights.claim: Tarlov says Jon Ossoff is winning by framing corruption as a scourge on the whole political class, focusing on Trump's crypto dealings, government contracts and unknown ballroom funders, while racking up Republican endorsements (including two big Republican mayors) on the strength of constituent service.
insights.speaker: Jessica Tarlov
insights.so_what: Ossoff is a template, and possibly a future presidential contender, for an anti-corruption platform that would target crypto and contracting conflicts.

insights.claim: Tarlov says Trump's refusal to acknowledge that the tariffs and the Iran war are hurting Americans is a key reason his support is eroding, and that Michigan in particular has been hurt by the tariffs, trade wars and the Iran war.
insights.speaker: Jessica Tarlov
insights.so_what: Tariff and war costs are now a political liability, which raises the odds of trade-policy reversal after the midterms.

insights.claim: Tarlov says Nick Fuentes was an early and accurate caller of Trump's weakness on the right, with Megyn Kelly and Tucker Carlson later following, signaling fracture within the MAGA coalition over unmet promises.
insights.speaker: Jessica Tarlov
insights.so_what: Intra-right fracture weakens Republican turnout and Trump's leverage over Congress.
insights.quote: he was definitely an early adopter of this is not what people were promised when they voted for Trump.

insights.claim: Tarlov says Democrats are winning the healthcare argument by 20-plus points, partly because Republicans have abdicated the issue: Trump has promised a healthcare plan for 10+ years without delivering, while the party voted dozens of times to repeal Obamacare.
insights.speaker: Jessica Tarlov
insights.so_what: A Democratic Congress would likely push drug-pricing, insurance-coverage and hospital-cost measures, a headwind for pharma, insurers and hospital systems.
insights.quote: Democrats are winning the healthcare argument by you know 20 plus points.

insights.claim: Tarlov cites a recent Wall Street Journal poll of the top 10 issues Democrats and Republicans agree on, in which roughly eight of the 10 concerned healthcare, and calls healthcare anxiety the most important element of politics.
insights.speaker: Jessica Tarlov
insights.so_what: Bipartisan agreement on healthcare costs makes pricing and claims-denial reform one of the few areas where legislation could actually pass.

insights.claim: Democratic candidates are explicitly campaigning against 'big pharma' and the 'hospital industrial complex', with Mark Cuban and his Cost Plus Drugs used as a campaign surrogate on affordable medicine alongside James Talarico in Texas.
insights.speaker: Jessica Tarlov
insights.so_what: Transparent-pricing, cost-plus drug models gain political tailwind while PBMs and pharma pricing face rising populist pressure.

insights.claim: Tarlov describes a split in Democratic healthcare messaging: Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan runs openly on universal health care, while Talarico in Texas promises no one loses coverage plus a more vibrant public option.
insights.speaker: Jessica Tarlov
insights.so_what: A public option is the more likely policy outcome than single-payer; private insurers should watch the public-option framing, not Medicare for All.

insights.claim: Tarlov says James Talarico's strategy is to turn Texas 'purple, not blue,' pitching against one-party rule that she says has left Texas with double the national uninsured rate, wages lagging the rest of the country and many farm bankruptcies.
insights.speaker: Jessica Tarlov
insights.so_what: A competitive Texas Senate race against Ken Paxton would be a major shift in the Senate map and in Texas policy risk.

insights.claim: Tarlov says Talarico has spoken out about protecting Texas's fossil fuel industry as the state's 'lifeblood' and as a jobs issue, and she argues that 'you don't have a green future unless you can keep the lights on'.
insights.speaker: Jessica Tarlov
insights.so_what: Even a Democratic Texas senator is unlikely to back hostile oil-and-gas policy, which limits downside regulatory risk for Texas energy producers.

insights.claim: Tarlov notes that Texas is also enormous in renewables and leading in wind and solar, something she says Trump does not want to acknowledge.
insights.speaker: Jessica Tarlov
insights.so_what: Texas renewables build-out continues despite federal hostility; a reminder that state grid economics drive deployment.

insights.claim: Tarlov says Gavin Newsom is pushing back against a proposed billionaires' tax and is in an internal fight with California Democrats such as Ro Khanna, whose Silicon Valley district she says has one of the highest concentrations of billionaires in the country.
insights.speaker: Jessica Tarlov
insights.so_what: Intra-party resistance from leading Democrats lowers the odds of an aggressive wealth tax even if Democrats gain power.

insights.claim: Tarlov frames Democratic billionaires such as Mark Cuban, JB Pritzker and Mike Bloomberg as backing the party on values, while progressive base voters push back on campaigning with them; Cuban joked at a Talarico event 'you're just going to eat me last'.
insights.speaker: Jessica Tarlov
insights.so_what: The tension between populist base and billionaire donors shapes how far Democratic tax proposals actually go.

insights.claim: Tarlov cites real-estate executive Ryan Serhant saying there are now only three markets, 'poor, rich and uncomfortable,' with even $1M earners squeezed by $75,000 private school and $2-3M two-bedroom apartments in big cities, and she argues progressive candidates are speaking to that discomfort.
insights.speaker: Jessica Tarlov
insights.so_what: An affordability squeeze reaching high earners widens the political base for cost-of-living populism (housing, healthcare, education).
insights.quote: there are only three markets right now poor rich and uncomfortable.

insights.claim: Tarlov says New York City spends roughly $52,000 per pupil, more than LA County or Chicago, while results sit in the bottom half of the country, and she pays about 52% in total taxes living in Manhattan, but argues Democrats want efficiency reform, not funding cuts.
insights.speaker: Jessica Tarlov
insights.so_what: High-tax blue-city spending efficiency is becoming a Democratic issue too, relevant to municipal fiscal and migration debates.

insights.claim: Tarlov says Democrats are abandoning purity tests and language policing because they cost elections and feed conservative media, describing a big-tent coalition from Abigail Spanberger to Zohran Mamdani focused on winning power.
insights.speaker: Jessica Tarlov
insights.so_what: A more pragmatic, centrist-tolerant Democratic Party lowers the odds of radical policy outcomes from a Democratic sweep.

themes.theme: Immigration and Crime: GOP's Remaining Edge

insights.claim: Tarlov says the most persuasive remaining Republican argument is immigration: despite a strong turn against ICE tactics, Democrats have not shown a solid enforcement plan, so pointing to Biden-era border chaos still persuades centrists.
insights.speaker: Jessica Tarlov
insights.so_what: Immigration remains the GOP's best issue, a key swing factor for the midterms and for detention and enforcement contractors.

insights.claim: Tarlov notes that even though murder rates and other crime metrics are down in big blue cities, voters still lack faith that Democrats will govern quality-of-life issues like crime, policing and homelessness effectively.
insights.speaker: Jessica Tarlov
insights.so_what: Perception lags data on urban crime; this is a political risk that keeps public-safety spending politically favored.
